body:
## Problem

Separation markers (`%=`) are ignored within item groups. This lead to a regression in Neovim 0.12 due to the overloaded item group syntax to set the ruler width: the `%=` works in the ruler, but not when the ruler is incorporated into the statusline where the item group syntax is interpreted in the usual way (because the ruler is now included as an expression, rather than pre-rendered by the ruler code), see #39984.

Truncation markers (`%<`) are not ignored within item groups, but only processed at the end outside of the group context, and only the first one actually has any effect. Meanwhile, item groups are always truncated from the left, regardless of included `%<`s. There is also a bug with `%<`s in hidden groups, see #39984. It would be more helpful if the truncation of each item group could be controlled separately.

## Solution

Allow %= in item groups (new feature). For example, the ruler expression in the default statusline `%-14.(%l,%c%V%)\ %P` can now be written `%18(%l,%c%V%=\ %P%)`, which actually works in both the statusline and the ruler, where it also sets the correct ruler width, and in vim, so it helps with shared configuration. It also becomes helpful when neither the left-aligned, nor the right-aligned part is of constant width, e.g. `%20(%l,%c%V%=\ %P%m%)`.

Scope %< to item groups and make top-level and group truncation consistent (breaking change). Now, groups are by default truncated at the first item, and truncation can be controlled for each item group separately:
```vim
set stl=%.15(%<path:\ %f%) " <th/to/file.txt (previous default without %<)
set stl=%.15(path:\ %<%f%) " path: <file.txt (new default without %<)
set stl=%.15(path:\ %f%<%) " path: /path/to>
```

Some minor edge-case issues were fixed along the way. See commit messages.

Remaining problem: I wanted to extend the tests from #21879. Unfortunately, they currently don't fail when the corresponding code is removed, at least not on my machine, and I don't know how to test this myself.

Addresses part of https://github.com/vim/vim/issues/2617

Fix #39984

Nice. Thanks again for your attention to detail here. The 'statusline' layer ('ruler', 'winbar', 'statuscolumn') is a very important component, which allows very flexible UI for plugins and core features (even cmdwin uses 'statuscolumn' now). So more attention in this area is really valuable.

Note: I squash merged because of "noise" commits like `remove duplicate test`. If you prefer not to squash merge, avoid "noise" commits.

@justinmk Very glad to be able to give something back! I love this project, and the more I look inside, the more I like the design decisions and how it's run!

Although I sometimes find the quirks of old software almost charming, some recent design decisions really motivated me to address some of my pet peeves :)

> even cmdwin uses 'statuscolumn' now

Nice, I'll have to look into that!

> very important component

It is basically most of the visible UI when you first open vim/nvim with default configuration. All the more surprising that I didn't find more complaints in neovim/vim issues/PRs/discussions related to many of the problems that I see. I suspect many of the people who realise that it can be configured either give up when they hit a roadblock or feel stupid when don't understand the behaviour, or they just content themselves with some compromise/workaround/extra plugin/distribution. In any case, I want to try and find ways of improving the documentation at some point.

> avoid "noise" commits

Noted.
